# R3 Gal 3:15–4:7 — Moo Galatians BECNT
**Range:** 3396–4049
**Lines actually read:** 3396–4049 (full exclusive slice; body through 4:7 Additional Notes; trailing outline headers 4038–4046)
**Claim count:** 42

## Claims

### C-R3-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, covenant, circumcision, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo frames 3:15–25 as continuing the case that “those who depend on faith” are Abraham’s sons; Paul separates faith from law-doing as a necessary accompaniment, insisting law-obedience is not required for justification and must not be required of Gentiles.
- **quote:** "obedience to the law is in no way a necessary requirement for justification, either in the present or in the future"
- **locus:** L3398
- **passage:** Gal 3:15–25 (intro)

### C-R3-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, covenant, circumcision, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** On Moo’s reconstruction, the agitators read the OT straightforwardly: Abraham’s faith was followed by circumcision (Gen 17) and eventually Mosaic law; Galatians as proselytes must complete faith with circumcision and law.
- **quote:** "like Abraham, they needed to follow up their faith with circumcision and obedience to the law of Moses"
- **locus:** L3400
- **passage:** Gal 3:15–18

### C-R3-003
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, abraham, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo says Paul places law and promise on different planes: the law could not alter the terms of God’s relationship with Abraham; key word in 15–18 (and beyond) is “promise.”
- **quote:** "Paul saw the law as operating on a different plane entirely. He insisted that the law could not alter the terms of the relationship that God had established with Abraham."
- **locus:** L3400
- **passage:** Gal 3:15–18

### C-R3-004
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo identifies two questions driving 19–25: why God gave the law if it added nothing material to the promise; and why Galatians could not keep obeying law as Paul redefined it—answered by law’s limited time until Messiah and by salvation-history shift at Christ’s coming.
- **quote:** "all along the law was intended to last only until the promised Messiah came"
- **locus:** L3402
- **passage:** Gal 3:19–25

### C-R3-005
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo treats ἀδελφοί and the question “Why then the law?” as bounding 15–18 as a paragraph; key claim is v. 17—promise covenant cannot be nullified by subsequent law; v. 16 is parenthetical in the paragraph’s logic.
- **quote:** "the key point comes in verse 17, where Paul claims that the promise God entered into with Abraham cannot be nullified by the subsequent law."
- **locus:** L3412
- **passage:** Gal 3:15–18

### C-R3-006
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo takes κατὰ ἄνθρωπον in 3:15 as neutral “everyday life” example (with Longenecker), not necessarily pejorative despite similar clauses in Rom 3:5 / 1 Cor 9:8.
- **quote:** "it is likely that he does so here in Gal. 3:15 also: thus R. Longenecker (1990: 127) paraphrases, “Let me take an example from everyday life.”"
- **locus:** L3414
- **passage:** Gal 3:15

### C-R3-007
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** For διαθήκη in 3:15, Moo prefers secular “will/testament” over biblical “covenant” because Paul cites a “human” arrangement, though he notes all other Pauline uses mean covenant including Gal 3:17; 4:24; the unchangeable nature of the agreement is what matters.
- **quote:** "διαθήκη in verse 15 has its other, “secular” meaning: “will” or “testament”"
- **locus:** L3418
- **passage:** Gal 3:15

### C-R3-008
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo reads 3:16 as identifying the διαθήκη of v. 17 with promises spoken to Abraham and his seed; “promise” well describes patriarchal blessings though ἐπαγγελία is rare in LXX patriarchal narratives; plural does not function differently from singular for Paul.
- **quote:** "Paul uses this aside to identify the “covenant” that he will be talking about in verse 17 with the “promises” that God gave to Abraham and to his seed."
- **locus:** L3420
- **passage:** Gal 3:16

### C-R3-009
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo thinks Gen 17 (esp. 17:8) is especially in view for “and to your seed” given covenant + seed collocation, though Gen 15:18 is also a candidate.
- **quote:** "The text of Gen. 17 may thus be the one that Paul has especially in view"
- **locus:** L3422
- **passage:** Gal 3:16

### C-R3-010
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, abraham, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo defends Paul’s singular “seed” = Christ: not merely forced modern reading; aligned with rabbinic technique; Paul knows collective sense (3:29); some Genesis texts use seed as semantic singular; Davidic seed traditions and salvation-history concentration in Christ warrant the move.
- **quote:** "Especially important is Paul’s reading of salvation history as the story of how God’s promises become concentrated in one person, Christ, the seed"
- **locus:** L3426
- **passage:** Gal 3:16

### C-R3-011
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, abraham, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo stresses Paul’s deliberate distinction of Abrahamic covenant/promise from Mosaic law: temporal priority (προκυρόω; 430 years later) means law cannot annul (ἀκυρόω) the prior covenant so as to nullify (καταργέω) the promise; promise activated by faith alone.
- **quote:** "the law… “came into the picture four hundred and thirty years after [the covenant].” This law, Paul notes, “does not annul”… the covenant"
- **locus:** L3428
- **passage:** Gal 3:17

### C-R3-012
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** In Additional Notes, Moo traces Paul’s “430 years” to Exod 12:40 (and Josephus Ant. 2.318) versus Gen 15:13’s 400 years; rabbis often applied 430 from Abrahamic covenant to law-giving; Paul may rely on that tradition.
- **quote:** "Paul’s figure of “four hundred and thirty years”… seems to be taken from Exod. 12:40"
- **locus:** L3504
- **passage:** Gal 3:17

### C-R3-013
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, justification, abraham, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo reads 3:18 as principle matching v. 17’s temporal argument: inheritance (κληρονομία) was graciously given (κεχάρισται) by promise; law’s “doing” principle is antithetical to promise’s grace (cf. Rom 4:4–5; 11:6).

- **locus:** L3430
- **passage:** Gal 3:18

### C-R3-014

### C-R3-015
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, abraham, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Against Jewish traditions of eternal law, Moo says Paul gives the law a definite beginning (“added” 430 years after promise; God as implied subject) and definite end—only until the seed (Christ) came.

### C-R3-016
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, justification, moo-galatians-becnt]

### C-R3-017
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** Moo rejects readings that distance the law from God via angels: διά is instrumental (“through angels”); mediator is Moses (ἐν χειρὶ idiom); angel involvement is traditional and not anti-divine; sets up v. 20 contrast.

- **locus:** L3442–L3444
- **passage:** Gal 3:19

### C-R3-018
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, covenant, moo-galatians-becnt]
- **claim:** For the notoriously difficult 3:20, Moo prefers the “two parties of mediation” view: a mediator implies two parties and human “doing”; promise involves the one God (Shema) in gift-character; he rejects strongly distancing God from the law.

- **locus:** L3450–L3454
- **passage:** Gal 3:20

### C-R3-019

## Coverage summary

- **3:15–18 (diathēkē / promise / 430 years):** Human διαθήκη as will/testament analogy; covenant = Abrahamic promise vs later law; parenthetical seed = Christ; 430 years from Exod 12:40 tradition; inheritance by gracious promise not law (C-R3-001–013).
- **3:19–25 (law’s purpose / paidagōgos):** Why the law—added for transgressions (sin → παράβασις), temporary until seed, through angels/Moses; not against promise; Scripture confines all under sin for faith-righteousness; “under law” custody; paidagōgos = child-supervisor with temporal limits, not schoolmaster-to-Christ; Additional Note on ὑπὸ νόμον (C-R3-014–028).
- **3:26–29 (sons / baptism / oneness):** Climax via union with Christ; sons by faith; water baptism as conversion capstone into Christ; Jew/Greek/slave/free/male-female adiaphorized not erased; seed/heirs in Christ (C-R3-029–034).
- **4:1–7 (minors / stoicheia / Abba):** Heir-as-slave under guardians until set time; stoicheia = material elements (with associated spirits), associated not equated with law; fullness of time; Son sent (preexistence likely), born under law, redeems for υἱοθεσία; Spirit of Son / Abba; son → heir through God (C-R3-035–042).
- **Moo definitions secured:** paidagōgos (C-R3-026–027); stoicheia (C-R3-037–038); ὑπὸ νόμον (C-R3-028); διαθήκη v. 15 (C-R3-007).
- **Not in range / not extracted as primary claims:** detailed MS apparatus except where Moo’s interpretive preference is load-bearing; full ancient-parallels note on 3:28; outline headers after 4:7.
